description:
FILED s532b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-06) while fixing #4163, whose filing guessed the opposite ("`package Q; our @INC` is @main::INC") -- perl 5.40.3 says otherwise.  PRE-EXISTING (59317afd the same).  LOW: rare, and a silent wrong only for a program that relies on it.

    perl -e 'package Q; our @INC; print \@INC == \@main::INC ? "same\n" : "diff\n";
             our %ENV; print \%ENV == \%main::ENV ? "esame\n" : "ediff\n";
             package R; print \@INC == \@main::INC ? "rsame\n" : "rdiff\n";'
    perl: diff / ediff / rdiff        (the alias stays in scope across `package R`)
    scratch/s532b/pr/p4163c.pl: `package Q; our @INC; print scalar(@INC) > 0 ? "inc-is-main" : "inc-empty"` -> perl inc-empty, PCL inc-is-main (same for %ENV).

perl: `our` adds a pad entry whose OURSTASH is PL_curstash and fetches the glob QUALIFIED with it (op.c / pad.c), so S_find_default_stash's forced-main list never applies.  An unqualified `@INC` with no `our` in scope is still @main::INC (that half is right in PCL).  Where: the `our` declaration's home in Parser2 (`_lower_our_decl`) and the binder's `our` record (Pl/Binder.pm's %SPECIAL_MAIN arm, ~line 653 -- s533d's region at the time of filing): an `our` binding of a forced-main name must home in the declaring package, and the uses it covers read that package's variable.  Probe: the three lines above + `our $_` (a lexical-ish special -- perl 5.40: `our $_` is allowed and is $main::_? probe it) + a sub reading the alias.


=== MEASURED (s536h) ===
MEASURED, NOT FIXED (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) -- two halves, and fixing either alone is worse than today:
(1) COMPILER: the use-site spelling of an `our` variable in a non-main package is FILE-WIDE, not scoped: Pl/ExprToCL.pm (the "Qualify `our` variables" arm, ~line 1529) asks Environment::is_our_variable(PKG, VAR), a set _lower_our_decl fills, so `package Q; push @INC, "x"; { our @INC; } print scalar(@INC)` emits Q::@INC for BOTH unqualified uses -- perl: both are main's @INC (no `our` in scope; probes scratch/s536h/p/m6b.pl, m6c.pl).  For an ordinary name this is harmless (an unqualified global in Q IS Q's); for a forced-main name it is the whole question.  The scoped answer is the binder's (Pl::Binder _resolve_ord: an `our` binding wins inside its range, else `special` -> main) -- s536e's region.
(2) RUNTIME / CL symbols: `Q::@INC` READS as pcl::@INC -- the user package :use's :pcl, which exports @INC / %ENV / @ARGV / ..., so `(defvar Q::@INC ...)` and every Q::@INC use are main's variable (m6a.pl rows 1-4, 6: perl diff / inc-empty / ediff / adiff / 0; PCL same / inc-is-main / esame / asame / 5).  Q needs its OWN symbol: a `(shadow ...)` of the inverted name in Q emitted (eval-always) BEFORE the first form that mentions Q::@INC -- the reader fixes the identity, so nothing at run time can.  %p-symref-intern already does exactly this for an explicitly qualified symbolic `@{"Q::INC"}` (the `foreign` shadow).
Today (1)'s mis-scoped uses are RIGHT BY ACCIDENT because of (2); shadowing alone would make them read Q's empty @INC.  Fix order: (1) first (ask the binder at the use site for a forced-main name), then (2) (emission change, generation bump), one batch.  `our $STDIN` (not exported from :pcl) already works.
subject: `package Q; our @INC;` (and `our %ENV`, `our @ARGV` ...) names the CURRENT package's variable in perl -- @Q::INC, empty -- but PCL aliases @main::INC: `our` bypasses gv.c's forced-main rule because it qualifies explicitly
